dialogues.speaker: Petit Lumiere
dialogues.text: Are you ready to make a Flash Cut?

response.speaker: Petit Lumiere
response.text: Alright, the cameras are in position and our actors are also ready to go. All you have to do is to do your thing.

choices.text: As for your plans for the future...

response.speaker: Petit Lumiere
response.text: I hope to get more trustworthy partners onboard, such as my older brother, Ms. Lepine-Pauline, and Mr. Xavier.

response.speaker: Petit Lumiere
response.text: You see, while the potential for Flash Cuts is indeed massive, the risks involved are equally substantial. Ms. Melies and I don't possess the necessary means to pull this off by ourselves.

response.speaker: Petit Lumiere
response.text: Of course, before moving forward, I must keep Ms. Melies on track, lest she deplete our entire budget all at once...

response.speaker: Petit Lumiere
response.text: Exactly. There's no need to rush. We've already established the direction for Flash Cuts, so all we have to do now is to move toward our goal, slowly but surely.

dialogues.speaker: Melies
dialogues.text: Oh hey there, my dearest partner! Are you here to shoot a Flash Cut?

response.speaker: Melies
response.text: Of course! Now that we've shown Flash Cuts to be a viable enterprise and have a future path, the future is bright, bright, bright!

response.speaker: Melies
response.text: Both the short-drama format of Flash Cuts and the ad-style Flash Cuts that was just proposed have the potential to take Fontaine by storm.

response.speaker: Melies
response.text: Now, all we need to do is take the plunge! We're set to become the biggest stars in all of Fontaine, no, the entire world.

response.speaker: Melies
response.text: And when that happens, we'll never have to worry about running out of Mora again... the crazy special effects no one wouldn't have touched before, the six-hour-long experimental films... There's light at the end of the tunnel now!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Just make sure you don't spend all your money in one go...

response.speaker: Melies
response.text: Oh, don't you worry about that! As Fontaine's most talented director, I can assure you my project management skills are equally top-notch. You can expect to hear good news from us!

choices.text: I'll leave you to it, then.

response.speaker: Melies
response.text: Bye! You can come by anytime. Maybe we'll have even better news for you the next time we see you!

dialogues.speaker: Petit Lumiere
dialogues.text: Are you ready to make a Flash Cut?

response.speaker: Petit Lumiere
response.text: Alright, the cameras are in position and our actors are also ready to go. All you have to do is to do your thing.

choices.text: As for your plans for the future...

response.speaker: Petit Lumiere
response.text: In my opinion, Flash Cuts is a creative format that hasn't quite achieved its ultimate state yet.

response.speaker: Petit Lumiere
response.text: At the risk of sounding a little self-aggrandizing, it is worth pointing out that both Ms. Melies and I are professional directors.

response.speaker: Petit Lumiere
response.text: From our approach to directing and shot composition to the use of special lighting effects, we both bring a particular perspective to the table. Therefore, the quality of our work naturally stands apart from that of the general public.

response.speaker: Petit Lumiere
response.text: However, I expect Flash Cuts to be something that everyone and anyone can create and appreciate. I foresee it to be a format that allows anyone to enjoy the appeal of making short films, regardless of when or where they are.

response.speaker: Petit Lumiere
response.text: Then, once we have sufficiently grown the public's appetite for Flash Cuts, the audience for traditional short films will also inevitably expand. Such a trend will, in turn, serve to elevate the industry as a whole.

response.speaker: Petit Lumiere
response.text: At least, I think so...

response.speaker: Petit Lumiere
response.text: Having said all that...

response.speaker: Petit Lumiere
response.text: We may have to devise more dynamic camera sequences so that we can formulate more templates for Flash Cuts.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That all sounds like a lot...

response.speaker: Petit Lumiere
response.text: I apologize. I was just speaking off the top of my head. I wasn't trying to cause you any stress. Right now, all I wish is for the two of you to revel in the creative satisfaction of crafting Flash Cuts.

response.speaker: Petit Lumiere
response.text: Just as you've noted, currently we don't really have a plot for Flash Cuts. This, admittedly, diverges from the conventional understanding of what a "film" is...

response.speaker: Petit Lumiere
response.text: As to how we can effectively have a storyline within the constraints of a Flash Cut, this is something I continue to investigate and explore.

response.speaker: Petit Lumiere
response.text: I'm not sure if you recall the first time we worked together. At that time, I suggested that you only need four shots to construct the smallest divisible unit of a story.

response.speaker: Petit Lumiere
response.text: And based on the experiment I just performed with Ms. Melies, I now believe that we can bring that number down to three.

response.speaker: Petit Lumiere
response.text: That is why all the scripts I've given you all ask for three shots or fewer.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: And how are the results so far?

response.speaker: Petit Lumiere
response.text: It remains a work in progress. As we don't have that many completed works at the moment, I have yet to come up with usable templates. As such, it'd be a great help if you could continue making more Flash Cuts.

response.speaker: Petit Lumiere
response.text: That's not a problem. Making Flash Cuts is all about giving free rein to your heart after all. You may begin whenever you're ready.

dialogues.speaker: Melies
dialogues.text: So how was it? Did you enjoy yourself while making the Flash Cut?

response.speaker: Melies
response.text: Really? Looks like I was right: there is indeed tremendous business potential for Flash Cuts...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Oh? Is there something I should know about?

response.speaker: Melies
response.text: Hehe, be patient, my dear partner. Right now, Flash Cuts is just a babe in arms that hasn't learned to walk yet.

response.speaker: Melies
response.text: If you ask me, while Flash Cuts are really engaging, we're still missing that meaningful content that actually touches the heart.

response.speaker: Melies
response.text: See, just like the Flash Cut we worked on together previously, although the battle scene was really spectacular, the dramatic scene was a little threadbare. That's why it ended up being just a so-so piece of work.

response.speaker: Melies
response.text: Who knows, maybe we can make a regular short film of better quality first, then edit the best parts of it into a Flash Cut for publicity purposes.

response.speaker: Melies
response.text: Or maybe, we can split the short film up into smaller units and release them one by one as standalone Flash Cuts. That should make for quite the viewing experience!

response.speaker: Melies
response.text: With a format like this, we might even be able to cut down on actor fees and use the savings towards props, the set, and special effects. That will improve the quality further!

response.speaker: Melies
response.text: But because something like this will cost comparatively less, I'll also be able to do more... We'll be able to do what might not be possible in the conventional film setting. Let's try it out and see how the market responds...

response.speaker: Melies
response.text: Come on, my dearest partner! Let's start shooting a Flash Cut now if we want to get a start on our bright, bright future!

choices.text: I should go. Sorry to bother you.

response.speaker: Melies
response.text: Don't worry about it. But do come by when you have the time so that we can build up our offering!
